cards.title: The Mirror Formula
cards.body: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f — where u is object distance, v is image distance, and f is focal length. For a concave mirror f is positive; for convex f is negative. All distances are from the mirror.

cards.title: Linear Magnification
cards.body: m = −v/u. The sign matters! A negative m means the image is inverted. |m| > 1 means magnified; |m| < 1 means diminished. An upright virtual image always has m > 0.

cards.title: The Concave Mirror
cards.body: A concave mirror curves inward — like the inside of a bowl. It bends all incoming rays toward a single point in front of the mirror called the Focal Point (F). f is positive.

cards.title: The Convex Mirror
cards.body: A convex mirror curves outward — like the back of a spoon. It spreads rays outward. f is negative. It always forms a smaller, upright virtual image — used in rear-view mirrors.

cards.title: Object Position Changes Everything
cards.body: Moving the object changes the size, location, and type of image. F (Focal Point) and C (Centre of Curvature, where C = 2F) divide the space — each region produces a different image.

cards.title: Real vs Virtual Images
cards.body: A real image forms where reflected rays actually meet in front of the mirror — v is positive, image is inverted, can be projected on a screen. A virtual image: v is negative, upright, seen behind mirror.

cards.title: How to Play
cards.body: Drag the white arrow left or right to move the object. The image updates live. Some missions ask you to calculate v and m using the formula — enter your answers in the panel below the diagram.

missions.title: Real Image — Guided
missions.learningGoal: Discover that a concave mirror forms a real image when the object is placed beyond the focal point.

payload.hint: Drag the object to the LEFT, past F. A real image forms when the object is beyond the focal point.

missions.title: Real Image — Magnified
missions.learningGoal: Understand that placing the object between F and C produces a magnified real image.

payload.hint: Place the object between F and C — the closer to F, the bigger the image.

missions.title: Real Image — Master
missions.learningGoal: Apply the mirror formula to produce exactly 2× magnification.

payload.hint: For 2× magnification, the image must be twice as far from the mirror as the object.

missions.title: Virtual Image — Guided
missions.learningGoal: Discover that virtual images form when the object is inside F or when using a convex mirror.

payload.hint: Try the convex mirror — it always forms upright virtual images. Or move the object inside F with a concave mirror.

missions.title: Virtual Image — Convex
missions.learningGoal: Understand that a convex mirror always forms a diminished virtual image.

payload.hint: Switch to the convex mirror. Move the object further away to make the image smaller.

missions.title: Virtual Image — Master
missions.learningGoal: Produce a precisely diminished virtual image using a convex mirror.

payload.hint: Convex mirror, object far from the mirror — the further away, the smaller the virtual image.

missions.title: Mirror Formula — First Calculation
missions.learningGoal: Apply 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = −v/u to calculate image distance and magnification.

payload.hint: Place the object at C (2F from mirror). A real same-size image forms there. Then use 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to calculate v.

missions.title: Mirror Formula — Magnified Image
missions.learningGoal: Calculate v and m for a magnified real image using the mirror formula.

payload.hint: Place the object between F and C so the image is magnified. Note the u value shown on the diagram, then calculate 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

missions.title: Magnification Challenge
missions.learningGoal: Calculate linear magnification m = −v/u, including the correct sign.

payload.hint: m = −v/u. Read the v value shown below the image arrow. Don't forget the negative sign — it tells you whether the image is upright or inverted.

missions.title: Dentist's Mirror
missions.learningGoal: Understand why a dentist's mirror produces a magnified upright virtual image of teeth.

payload.hint: A dentist's mirror is concave, held so the tooth is inside F. The image appears upright and magnified behind the mirror. Move the object inside F to see this.

missions.title: Rear-View Mirror
missions.learningGoal: Explain why a convex rear-view mirror gives a wide field of view but makes objects look smaller.

payload.hint: A rear-view mirror is always convex — objects appear smaller and upright. Move the object far away to simulate a car far behind.

missions.title: Telescope Mirror
missions.learningGoal: Produce a large real image as a concave reflecting telescope mirror would for a distant star.

payload.hint: A reflecting telescope uses a large concave mirror to gather and focus starlight. Place the object just outside F to get a large, inverted real image — this is where the eyepiece would be placed.
